blocks.text: Hillcrest staging-per-client design

This is the working cut for HIL-TDD-2025-009 on February 6, 2025. Keisha Ward asked for a written bound after the current path (Ad-hoc previews, one leftover shared host) stopped being honest. I am Michael Gilfilian, Web Developer, writing for Aisha Rahman, Sam Reid, and Keisha Ward. Primary host stg-router.hillcrest.internal. If you are skimming, jump the decision callout, then the refuse on one shared preview.hillcrest.internal for every client, then open questions. If you are implementing next week, jump the constraints, the numbers table, and the commands or contracts.

DNS stg-<client>.hillcrest.internal. Separate Shopify preview or Woo staging. Shared leftover preview is out. Basic auth plus VPN. I am not restating a hallway yes. one shared preview.hillcrest.internal for every client is out because January leftover mixed Harbor gift-card copy into a Lakeshore preview. Keisha caught it before Luis did. Cost of doing nothing is already in the numbers: look at clients=2, mixed=1, weeks=4, hosts=2, auth=1, vpn=1, leftover=1, dns=1. Sibling tickets HIL-2318 and HIL-SOP-2024-031. I will not reopen one shared preview.hillcrest.internal for every client in a side thread because a vendor sent a discount. Sam Reid is the acceptor unless the owners line says otherwise.
Decision for leadership

Ticket HIL-TDD-2025-009 names the pull. If those numbers moved after February 6, 2025, update this file in review, do not 'correct' them in Slack.

blocks.text: Background. Why the current path is the wrong tool

Keisha Ward owns a leftover that is easy to skip: stg-lakeshore.hillcrest.internal. I will ping once. After that the owner is late, not blocked. Unique to this file (49): refuse on one shared preview.hillcrest.internal for every client, lock is per-client host, basic auth, VPN, no shared preview. I will not hide a product change inside a 'quick align' on HIL-2318.
If Dana can see Luis's unpublished theme because we reused a preview, we failed onboard.

What a skeptical user would try first on stg-router.hillcrest.internal: the path Keisha Ward actually has, not a desktop demo. Metric I will argue is time-to-useful, not a vanity QPS. If we cannot show that path on stg-harbor.hillcrest.internal with the numbers already in this file, we do not have a cut. Michael Gilfilian will not accept a laptop screenshot as that proof.
Constraints and the lock

blocks.label: Lock
blocks.text: per-client host, basic auth, VPN, no shared preview Host stg-router.hillcrest.internal. Ticket HIL-2318. Acceptor Aisha Rahman.

Open clock: per-client host, basic auth, VPN, no shared preview. If that clock collides with a freeze, the date moves and the scope does not. Aisha Rahman hears the new date on HIL-TDD-2025-009. I will not book a change in the last 40 minutes of a freeze because it is 'just config.' Config is a change. Host if we have to prove a count: stg-router.hillcrest.internal.

I want that named in review notes, not rediscovered by Keisha Ward on a Monday. Ticket HIL-2318. Numbers I will not 'simplify': clients=2, mixed=1, weeks=4, hosts=2, auth=1, vpn=1, leftover=1, dns=1. Same clock as the front. I will not mix clocks to make stg-router.hillcrest.internal look healthier.

What I will not claim in HIL-TDD-2025-009

I will not claim one shared preview.hillcrest.internal for every client is impossible for a competitor. I will claim we will not buy it. I will not claim zero incidents after this cut. I will claim the next one dies at the gate named in the lock. Host stg-router.hillcrest.internal.
First useful slice for HIL-2318

First useful is per-client host, basic auth, VPN, no shared preview, not a prettier theme or a bigger box. Keisha Ward sees that slice on stg-router.hillcrest.internal. If the slice needs a second product, that is a new ticket and Aisha Rahman is in the thread. I will not hide it inside HIL-TDD-2025-009.
